fixed_statement:
- Consider a two-cell model with two oriented \(2\)-cells \(A,A'\) satisfying \(f_\#A=f_\#A'=P\).
- Let \(N=A-A'\).
- Suppose an exact-plaque bad set contains \(A\) but not \(A'\), and let \(P_{\rm bad}\) be the source-local projection with \(P_{\rm bad}A=A\), \(P_{\rm bad}A'=0\).

In the two-cell model,
\[
N\in\ker f_\#,
\qquad
f_\#P_{\rm bad}N=P\ne0.
\]
fixed_proof: Since \(f_\#A=f_\#A'=P\), one has \(f_\#N=0\). But \(P_{\rm bad}N=A\), so \(f_\#P_{\rm bad}N=P\ne0\). Dually, a quotient cochain has equal values on \(A\) and \(A'\), and restriction to the nonsaturated bad set changes one value but not the other. Thus exact source localization and quotient invariance are in tension.
reason: Moved the derivational and dual explanatory material out of the statement into the proof, and removed the vague/meta commentary about obtaining \((\mathrm{EAT})\) “without a new idea” and the unrelated proof-needs commentary.
